reason: This passage (Exodus 2:11-15) depicts individual acts of Moses rather than a portrayal of the Hebrews as a nation engaged in political struggle. While the text establishes the context of Hebrew oppression (they bear burdens under Egyptian taskmasters), it does not show coordinated national political resistance. Instead, it focuses on: (1) Moses' personal observation of oppression, (2) his individual act of violence against an Egyptian, (3) a personal confrontation between two Hebrew men, and (4) Moses' flight. The passage contains no religious or cosmic language either. The portrayal is of individual ethical action and personal authority in response to oppression, not of a nation in a collective political fight for liberty.
